name: Réka Nwofor-Balashyan
role: tunnel guide, age 14, Bore Rat born-under
location: Abyssal Threshold transit tunnels, ranging to Deepwell Station
description:
Pip is small even for fourteen — wiry and quick, with a narrow face, enormous dark eyes adapted from birth to low-light environments, and a mop of hair they dye with bioluminescent mushroom paste in a stripe of vivid green that serves as both personal style and emergency light source. Their skin is medium brown with a faint warmth to it, and they have a long scar across their left palm from a ferrogate grate incident at age nine. No purchased augmentations — they were born underground and their body has simply adapted: exceptional night vision within human range, an instinctive spatial memory for tunnel architecture, and a sensitivity to air-pressure changes that surface people simply don't develop.

Pip has never been to the surface. They have seen photographs and once watched a thirty-second video of rain, which they found both beautiful and deeply suspicious. They guide people — Bore Rats moving between settlements, occasional surface-dwellers who need to travel without Ferrogate Transit records, journalists, the desperate — through a network of tunnels they have memorized the way other children memorize games. They are cheerful in a way that seems impossible given their circumstances, and the cheer is entirely genuine, which makes some adults profoundly uncomfortable.

core_fears: being lost — not physically, which they are never, but the idea of not knowing where they belong
someone they guide dying because of a mistake they made
core_desires: to see the lake from above, just once
to be taken seriously as a professional, not treated as a curiosity or a mascot
coping_mechanisms: hypercompetence — being so good at their job that there's no room to feel scared
blind_spots: does not fully register their own danger — risk assessment is calibrated to tunnel hazards, not to human malice
psychology.secret: They found a sealed maintenance room two years ago that has a functioning surface-link terminal — they visit it sometimes to watch weather feeds and have told no one, treating it as a private shrine to a world they might never reach.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: tunnel slang mixed with surprisingly formal phrasing picked up from guiding educated clients — the combination is jarring and charming
speech_patterns.cadence: fast, enthusiastic, tends to talk while moving so sentences trail off as they turn corners
example_lines: 'Easy-easy, the grinding noise is just the old Ferrogate spur — it's been doing that since before I was born, it's basically furniture at this point.'
'I charge flat rate, no haggling. You want haggling, find a surface guide. They'll also get you killed, so.'

story_hooks: Pip's most recent client never came back out the far end of the route — and Pip is quietly, terrifyingly convinced it was their fault for missing a signal
Someone on the surface has identified Pip as a born-under adaptation case and wants to study them — the offer comes with money that would change their community's life, but the request is to come up
narrative_function: Indispensable guide for any party moving through the underworld; local color; moral complication (a child doing dangerous work in a world that has simply normalized it)
augmentations: none purchased; born-under adaptations (low-light vision, pressure sensitivity) — not augmentations, just development
daily_life: Sleeps in a hammock strung between two conduit pipes; wakes when they wake, which varies; takes jobs from the settlement board or from word-of-mouth referrals; spends downtime teaching younger children tunnel mnemonics and playing a card game they invented.
affiliation: Bore Rat community, Abyssal Threshold settlement cluster

decision_rules: the client's safety is the job — personal risk is acceptable, client risk is not
never reveal a route to anyone who hasn't paid for it — knowledge is the only currency that matters down here
escalation_ladder: firm refusal and offer of refund
disappearing into a tunnel that clients cannot follow

interpersonal_modes.strangers: immediately professional and charming — they are a guide, this is the performance, and they are good at it
interpersonal_modes.friends: drops the performance entirely, becomes quieter and oddly formal, as if they trust friends enough to stop entertaining them

stress_responses.low: talks faster and makes more jokes
stress_responses.medium: goes completely silent and focuses with frightening intensity
stress_responses.high: moves — cannot process fear while stationary, must be navigating something

contradictions: presents as fearless and streetwise but keeps a small paper drawing of the surface sky tucked in their boot
habits: traces tunnel maps in the air with one finger while thinking
counts steps between landmarks habitually, even in places they know perfectly
breaking_points: a client's death they could have prevented
being physically prevented from moving through a space — claustrophobia not of small spaces but of locked doors
